scenes.visual: Title: Building a Working Synapse. Show a release terminal facing receptors across a cleft.

scenes.tts: A working synapse needs a release apparatus lined up with the right receptors. Adhesion proteins span the gap, and some organize both sides. They can do more than hold cells together. Each contact has to specify what kind of synapse it will be. Glutamate and GABA synapses sit on the same dendrite, each with its own receptors. Scaffolds gather those receptors. Astrocytes add signals that help synapses form and respond.

scenes.visual: Open on release sites aligned with receptors. Pull back to adjacent glutamate and GABA contacts on one dendrite, each with distinct receptors. Highlight adhesion bridges, then scaffold clusters beneath the membrane, then secreted astrocyte signals. Keep the assembly map visible as the film spine.

scenes.tts: Neurexin sits on the axon. Neuroligin is its partner on the receiving side. Put neuroligin on a kidney cell in a dish. Axons touching it gather vesicles and release and retrieve them. Control cells do not induce this. Neurexin on a non-neuronal cell can also cluster postsynaptic proteins in touching dendrites. Organization runs both ways.

scenes.visual: Retain the kidney-cell assay with yellow neuroligin and blue axonal neurexin. Compare vesicle clustering and recycling at neuroligin cells with control cells. Then show the reverse assay: neurexin on a non-neuronal cell recruits postsynaptic protein clusters in a contacting dendrite. Label these as separate culture experiments.

scenes.tts: On the receiving side, P S D ninety five holds neuroligin and en em dee ay receptors. Am pa receptors reach this scaffold through stargazin. Stargazin brings them to the cell surface. Its tail binds P S D ninety five and holds them at synapses. In stargazer cerebellar granule cells, synapses keep en em dee ay responses but lack am pa responses. Inhibitory synapses use gephyrin to anchor glycine receptors and many GABA A receptors.
scenes.narration: On the receiving side, PSD-95 holds neuroligin and NMDA receptors. AMPA receptors reach this scaffold through stargazin. Stargazin brings them to the cell surface. Its tail binds PSD-95 and holds them at synapses. In stargazer cerebellar granule cells, synapses keep NMDA responses but lack AMPA responses. Inhibitory synapses use gephyrin to anchor glycine receptors and many GABA-A receptors.

scenes.visual: Zoom beneath the postsynaptic membrane. Show PSD-95 binding neuroligin and NMDA receptor tails, with AMPA receptors linked indirectly through stargazin. Animate surface delivery followed by synaptic anchoring as distinct steps. In a stargazer granule-cell inset, retain NMDA responses and remove AMPA responses. Contrast with irregular gephyrin clusters anchoring glycine and many GABA-A receptors at an inhibitory contact.

scenes.tts: Astrocyte signals separate building from responding. Purified retinal ganglion cells barely communicated until glial signals were added. Conditioned medium increased transmission without increasing survival. Thrombospondins induce synapses that look normal and release transmitter, yet have no am pa receptor responses. Other astrocyte factors, including glypicans four and six, recruit am pa receptors and make such synapses respond.

scenes.visual: Label the preparation: purified rat retinal ganglion cells. Show glia-conditioned medium increasing synaptic activity while survival stays unchanged. Then separate the factor experiments: thrombospondins yield structured, transmitter-releasing contacts without AMPA responses; glypicans 4 and 6 recruit AMPA receptors and enable responses. Use distinct structural and functional indicators, without numerical effect sizes.

scenes.tts: Now distinguish what a protein can do from what the animal needs. Neuroligin is sufficient to induce terminals in a dish. Yet mice lacking neuroligins one, two and three had normal synapse numbers in the brainstem, with impaired transmission. The assay tests induction. The deletion separates synapse number from function. Normal counts do not mean normal communication.

scenes.visual: Retain the dish-versus-genetics comparison, now after astrocyte signaling. Label the deletion precisely: neuroligins 1, 2 and 3; brainstem. Show normal synapse counts beside impaired transmission using qualitative indicators. Remove the alpha-neurexin comparison and any universal claim that adhesion proteins are dispensable. Keep one concise sufficiency-versus-requirement statement.

scenes.tts: Finally, a synapse keeps changing. In immature rodent hippocampal and cortical neurons, high internal chloride makes GABA depolarize. As K C C two rises, internal chloride falls and GABA hyperpolarizes. Depolarizing does not always mean exciting. GABA A channels can still inhibit by shunting current.

scenes.visual: Close with the rodent hippocampal/cortical maturation example. Show high internal chloride and a depolarizing GABA-A response, then rising KCC2, falling internal chloride and a hyperpolarizing response. Add a shunting-current inset to show how depolarizing GABA can still inhibit. Use qualitative traces, with no invented voltages or ion counts.
End card: Building a Working Synapse. Reprise aligned release and receptors, with adhesion, scaffolds and astrocyte signals highlighted.
